summary: Richard Hauschild was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen, Leipzig, and Jena under Johannes Hertel and Albert Debrunner. He was a professor at the University of Jena (1951–1967) and a member of the Saxon Academy of Sciences (1949–1972).

Richard Henebry was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at St. John's College, Waterford, St Patrick's Pontifical University, the University of Greifswald, and the University of Freiburg, where he studied under Heinrich Zimmer from circa 1895 to 1898.

Richard Hugh Robinson worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Alberta and London under Arthur Waley, David Friedman, and David Snellgrove, he taught at Toronto (1954) and became a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1961.

Richard Hughes Seager is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD). He served as Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College from circa 1994 to 2014.

Richard J. Davidson studied at New York University and Harvard University before spending his career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he served as a psychology professor from 2001 to 2017.

Richard Jay Kohn was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1988 under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, also studying under Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

Richard K. Payne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. He served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies around 1995 and was later named Professor Emeritus at the Numata Center.
Richard Keith Sprigg was a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at Oakham School. He held academic posts at the University of London and SOAS University of London from circa 1948 to 1980.

Richard Kieckhefer is a historian and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Saint Louis University and the University of Texas at Austin. He became a professor of history and religious studies at Northwestern University in 1975.

Richard King is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster. He held posts at the University of Stirling, Vanderbilt University (circa 2003–2011), and the University of Glasgow (circa 2011).

Richard M. Jaffe is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held a position at North Carolina State University from circa 1995 to 2000 before becoming Professor of Religious Studies at Duke University around 2000.

Richard Mahoney is a scholar in Buddhist and computational studies. He completed a Master of Arts under Paul Harrison at the University of Canterbury by 2002, where he also held a post attested in 2001.

Richard Morris was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Battersea Training College. He served as Winchester lecturer at King's College School (1869), master at Dedham Grammar School, and headmaster of the Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875–1888).

Richard N. Frye was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and history. After studying at Illinois and Harvard, he worked for the OSS and held posts at Harvard (circa 1948–1990), Frankfurt, and Hamburg.

Richard P. Boyle conducted graduate work at the University of Washington and studied under Kyozan Joshu Sasaki. He held a teaching post at UCLA and an affiliation with the University of New Mexico attested in 2015.

Richard P. Hayes is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who earned his doctorate at Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He taught at McGill (attested 1997–2009) and the University of New Mexico (attested 2011–2016).

Richard Payne is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996, 2007) and held a post at the University of Chicago (attested 2021).

Richard Phené Spiers was an architectural historian and archaeologist who studied at King's College London from circa 1856 to 1858 and at the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts from circa 1858 to 1861.

Richard Pischel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. He held professorships at Kiel (1875), Halle (1885–1902), and Berlin (1902–1908), and served as Rektor at Halle-Wittenberg.

Richard Polenberg was an American history scholar who studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University. He served as Professor of American History at Cornell University from 1966 to 2011 and was a Fulbright Visiting Professor at Hebrew University.
